---
title: "Margins and Perceptron"
---

This lecture prepares students for support vector machines by focusing
on linear decision boundaries, margins, and simple iterative learning
rules.

## Learning Objectives

- Describe a linear classifier as a separating hyperplane.
- Explain the perceptron update rule.
- Connect classification mistakes to loss functions.
- Use margins to reason about classifier robustness.

## Core Ideas

The perceptron is useful pedagogically because it makes classification
geometry visible. A point is misclassified when the sign of
$x_i^\top w$ does not match its label, and the update moves the
boundary toward a better separation.

For labels $y_i \in \{-1, 1\}$, the perceptron predicts using

$$
\hat y_i = \operatorname{sign}(w^\top x_i + b).
$$

When observation $i$ is misclassified, the weights are updated as

$$
w \leftarrow w + \eta y_i x_i,
\qquad
b \leftarrow b + \eta y_i,
$$

where $\eta$ is a learning rate. The update moves the boundary in the
direction that would make the current example more likely to be
classified correctly.

## Margins

A margin measures how far an observation is from the decision boundary.
Large margins are desirable because small perturbations to the data are
less likely to change the predicted class. This idea leads directly to
support vector machines, which choose a separating boundary by
maximizing the margin while allowing controlled violations.

```r
set.seed(571)
x1 <- rnorm(100)
x2 <- rnorm(100)
y <- factor(ifelse(x1 + x2 + rnorm(100, sd = 0.5) > 0, "A", "B"))
plot(x1, x2, col = y, pch = 19)
```

## Worked Example

Start with a two-dimensional synthetic data set. Animate or step through
updates, then compare the learned boundary with logistic regression and
a hard-margin classifier when separation is possible.

## Applied Practice

Practice by drawing a two-dimensional classification data set, fitting
a linear classifier, and identifying points close to the decision
boundary. Explain how changing the margin or allowing violations would
change the fitted boundary.
